items.titleEn: Samsung, SK Hynix stocks plunge sharply: why over $8 billion has not calmed markets
items.summaryEn: Buy. The selloff is being driven by AI sentiment and foreign outflows, not by collapsing orders: Samsung says next-year high-bandwidth memory supply is effectively sold out. With KOSPI down sharply and a government backstop signaling potential stabilization, the stock is set up for a fast mean-reversion once panic selling slows. Key catalyst is that order visibility (scarcity) should cap downside even if the market is volatile. Key Risk: AI data-center spending gets delayed and Samsung is forced to cut memory prices despite “sold out” supply claims. Buy. SK Hynix has contracts with 14 major customers covering more than half of planned 2027–2028 capacity, which should protect earnings power through the next cycle. The current drop is amplified by a Wall Street semiconductor rout and foreign selling, while fundamentals (customer coverage) argue the market is overshooting. Expect stabilization as oversold conditions meet any support-fund headlines.

items.titleEn: Nvidia stock: Trump pushes for Jensen Huang's return, but will the board listen?
items.summaryEn: Buy NASDAQ:NVDA. The selloff is being driven by governance noise (CEO reinstatement fight) plus headline regulatory risk (SEC/accounting probe, China/export-control questions). Meanwhile, fundamentals are still accelerating: fiscal Q3 revenue $115.8B (+103%) and data-center sales $107.6B (+110%), with Q4 guidance around $130B. If the board holds the line, the market can still re-rate on earnings power and AI demand staying intact; a named CEO outcome is a catalyst, not the core driver. Key Risk: A real, material regulatory/accounting finding that forces restatements, fines, or blocks China-related revenue. Sell NASDAQ:NVDA short. The thesis is that governance uncertainty will persist: interim CEO (Colette Kress), board refusal to reinstate Huang, and an SEC investigation create a long “overhang” that keeps multiples compressed even if revenue is strong. If investors fear engineering churn or customer pauses while compliance questions linger, the stock can stay in a penalty box until leadership and regulatory clarity arrive.

items.titleEn: Nvidia faces US accounting probe amid deepening turmoil
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported Saturday, citing people briefed on the confidential investigation.

items.titleEn: Will Jensen Huang's ouster push founders to secure more voting rights?
items.summaryEn: Buy Meta (META). If founders respond to Huang’s ouster by pushing for more control, the market will reward companies with proven, durable governance that already concentrates voting power (Zuckerberg’s dual-class). META’s structure reduces the chance of disruptive governance fights during leadership crises, supporting steadier execution and capital allocation. Key Risk: Regulators or investors successfully pressure Meta to unwind dual-class voting, or a major governance/legal event forces a structural change. Sell NVDA. The article frames Huang’s exit as a national-security/espionage narrative that governance (even dual-class) can’t fix. That keeps a credibility and execution overhang on the new leadership, even with strong near-term results. The market will keep discounting “key-person + investigation risk” until the probe outcome is clean.
